notes: Adds FindAllImportStatements with the same ConfigResource-level ancestor override as C1, so cross-module different-instance imports are still dropped; it also keeps the old map-returning function as a now-unused API that is lossy by design.

Fixes the root-module case. It still deduplicates parent and child imports by config resource, so a child import for a different instance than the parent's is silently dropped. It also leaves the old map-based FindImportStatements unused, with a comment admitting it discards blocks.

Fixes the reported root-module case by returning a slice, but it still drops every child-module import for a resource when the parent imports any instance of that resource, which is the same silent-drop bug in the cross-module case.

Clean slice-based fix for same-module blocks. Parent/child override is still keyed on the config resource, so child imports for different instances are lost. The new unit test codifies that incorrect cross-module behavior.

Returns all statements and dedups parent-over-child per instance by parsing the static `to` address, which handles cross-module different-instance imports; however, it reimplements expansion logic statically, treats any dynamic (for_each) parent import as overriding all child imports, and can mismatch on keyed module instances.

Compares each block against all prior statements at the statically parsed instance level, which correctly handles the issue and parent/child different-instance cases. Unlike the reference's expansion-time dedupe, it is conservative with dynamic for_each targets and keyed module instances, which likely explains the one failing hidden test.

Uses an instance-level static override like C2, but it compares only against the single last-claimed statement per resource, so a parent with multiple instance imports, or interleaved child imports, can fail to override the matching child block; it has good root and module integration tests.

Instance-level static dedupe is the right idea and handles the issue and the different-instances module case. However, `claimed` only holds the last kept statement per resource, so a parent/child duplicate can slip through and the child then overwrites the parent at expansion. Dynamic `to` addresses fall back to dropping the child's blocks.
